No convention findings: nothing in this change breaks any of the 78 rules in `docs/engineering/sources/rules.json`.

**Mode:** `--review-pr`. I regenerated the checklist and considered every item (78 of 78 marked checked). The checklist file is git-ignored and untracked, and no tracked files were changed.

**Scope:** `git diff d0e03bb0b...HEAD` is a single commit, `e7c495346 ci: Drop Docker Hub -> GHCR tag mirror`. It deletes `.github/workflows/mirror-to-ghcr.yml` (170 lines removed, nothing added).

**Rules that applied, and why each passes:**
- **CI-01** (concurrency scoping), **CI-02** (release workflows), **CI-03** (codegen drift) and **CI-04** (`permissions: {}` needs `contents: read`): these only matter for workflows being added or edited. Removing a manually triggered one-off workflow changes no concurrency, release or permission setup elsewhere.
- **API-01** (search consumers when removing something) and **DOC-02** (operational docs): `git grep` finds no remaining references to `mirror-to-ghcr`, to "Mirror Docker Hub" or to its destination image outside `docs/engineering`. No docs or other workflows depend on it.
- **REVIEW-01** (don't mix unrelated changes into CI PRs): the change touches one CI file and nothing else.
- **DOC-01**, **TEST-04**, **SEC-02** and **PROD-01**: none apply. There are no docs, tests, runtime code, destructive runtime actions or user-facing behaviour in the diff.
- All web, mobile, state, data, transaction, UI and end-to-end test rules: no surface in this diff.

**Rules that led to changes:** none, since this was a read-only review. I didn't need to look up any rule's history (no Level 1 or Level 2 zoom).

**Open question (not a rule failure):** the deleted file's header said "Delete once the Docker Hub migration is signed off." Nothing in the repo records that sign-off, so the PR description should confirm it happened. Otherwise tags that were never copied to GHCR can't be re-mirrored without restoring the workflow from `322235464` (#8710).
